profile.size: Large billfish; anglers target numbers on light tackle rather than size
profile.swimming_depth: Mostly the upper 20 m, with repeated short dives to 50-150 m below the thermocline (Gulf of Mexico and Florida Straits tagging)
profile.behavior: Stays above the thermocline in about 21-28 C water. In winter along the Florida coast the fish travel just outside the outer reef line, often along the green-to-blue water edge; cold fronts concentrate them.
profile.regulations_note: Atlantic billfish need a NOAA Fisheries permit for fishing in federal waters, and state rules may also apply. Check before you fish.

factors.value_notes: Tagging records off Florida's east coast (2003-2018): sailfish were caught at 26.2 C on average (SD 1.7), most often at 25.2-25.5 C, with catches rising from 26 to 29 C and no change near 25 or 30 C. Satellite tags in the SW Atlantic put fish in 26-28 C most of the time. Florida Museum: usually above the thermocline in 70-83 F (21-28 C). The ideal band is an interpretation of these.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside the {ideal_min}-{ideal_max} C range where sailfish are most often found.

factors.value_notes: South Florida angling accounts put winter sailfish on the green-to-blue color change and temperature edges just outside the reef line, and cold fronts concentrate them. Scored relative to today's sharpest offshore breaks. Needs calibration against catch reports.
factors.reason_template: Water temperature changes about {per10km} C every 10 km here, one of the sharper breaks in the area today. Sailfish travel along color and temperature edges.

factors.value_notes: Only a rough guide: a SW Atlantic study found adult sailfish most frequent at 0.3-0.8 mg/m3 chlorophyll, and Florida anglers look for the blue side of the green-to-blue edge. Different ocean and method, so the band is a placeholder.
factors.reason_template: Chlorophyll is {value} mg/m3, around the blue-water edge sailfish favor.

factors.value_notes: Florida accounts describe winter sailfish along the outer reef line in about 100-300 ft (30-90 m), with a late-season color change in 70-250 ft. Cells shallower than 20 m are excluded (inshore of the reef line). Numbers are provisional.
factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in the reef-line and shelf-edge water where sailfish travel.

factors.value_notes: South Florida's sailfish season runs about November to March. Peak is usually after the first of the year (January is cited as the peak), when cold fronts arrive every 5-7 days. Sailfish can be caught year-round in smaller numbers. Mild winters with few cold fronts spread the fish out.

value_text.peak: It is peak sailfish season (about December to February), when cold fronts concentrate the fish.
value_text.in_season: It is sailfish season (about November to March) in South Florida.
value_text.off: It is outside the main sailfish season (November to March), so far fewer fish are in South Florida.

factors.value_notes: Cold fronts concentrate sailfish. Not yet detected by the pipeline (planned).
The western edge of the Gulf Stream is where many winter sailfish are found. Planned with current data.
